paragraphs.title: The Women Seeking to Remove Their Shame

easy.explanation: Isaiah 4:1 says, “seven women shall take hold of one man.”
easy.q: How many women shall take hold of one man?

easy.explanation: They say, “only let us be called by thy name.”
easy.q: What do the women ask to be called by?

easy.explanation: They say, “We will eat our own bread, and wear our own apparel.”
easy.q: What are the women willing to provide for themselves?

medium.explanation: They ask this “to take away our reproach.”
medium.q: Why do the women ask to be called by the man's name?

answers: There will be more men than women
All the men will leave willingly
medium.explanation: The unusual situation suggests that many men will be absent or dead after calamity.
medium.q: What situation is suggested by seven women seeking one man?
In this verse, what does “reproach” most nearly mean?

answers: They demand that the man support them
They give up material support and seek social belonging
They do not want any relationship with the man
challenge.explanation: They will provide their own food and clothing and ask mainly to be called by his name.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the women's statement about bread and apparel?

answers: The calamity has produced an extreme imbalance between women and men
The judgment has made clothing unavailable
The judgment has removed the need for marriage
challenge.explanation: The verse presents an unusual social condition in which seven women seek one man.
challenge.q: How does the condition described in verse 1 relate to the surrounding judgment?

answers: A desire for recognized belonging and marital identity
A request for food and clothing
challenge.explanation: Their request centers on being identified with the man and having their reproach removed.
challenge.q: What is the central meaning of “only let us be called by thy name”?

short_answers.question: What do the women want removed?
short_answers.explanation: They want their shame or disgrace taken away.

paragraphs.title: The Purification and Holiness of Jerusalem's Remnant

easy.explanation: The verse says, “the branch of the Lord be beautiful and glorious.”
easy.q: What shall the branch of the Lord be in that day?
What shall the fruit of the earth be?

easy.explanation: The one who remains in Zion “shall be called holy.”
easy.q: What shall the one left in Zion be called?

answers: Beauty and fruitfulness, a holy remnant, and cleansing
medium.explanation: The passage moves from the Lord's beauty and the earth's fruit to a holy remnant and cleansing.
medium.q: What is the main sequence of events in these verses?

answers: The person who remains in Zion
The person who rules outside Zion
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to someone who remains in Zion after judgment.
medium.q: What does “he that is left in Zion” mean?

answers: By the spirit of judgment and the spirit of burning
medium.explanation: Verse 4 speaks of cleansing “by the spirit of judgment, and by the spirit of burning.”
medium.q: By what means is Jerusalem cleansed?

answers: The remnant is called holy after filth and blood are purged
Holiness refers only to the fruit of the earth
challenge.explanation: The passage connects the holiness of the remnant with the removal of filth and blood.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between holiness and cleansing in this passage?

answers: They symbolize beauty, glory, excellence, and restoration
They are presented as causes of judgment
They serve only as protection from rain
challenge.explanation: The branch is beautiful and glorious, while the fruit is excellent and comely.
challenge.q: How do the branch and the fruit contribute to the passage's message?

answers: It remains in Jerusalem and is called holy after evil is purged
It asks only for food and clothing
challenge.explanation: Those who remain are written among the living and are called holy after cleansing.
challenge.q: What distinguishes the remnant from the condition described before cleansing?

short_answers.question: What two things are purged from Jerusalem?
short_answers.answer: The filth of the daughters of Zion and the blood of Jerusalem.
short_answers.explanation: Verse 4 says the Lord will wash away the filth and purge the blood.

paragraphs.title: God's Glory and Protection over Zion

easy.explanation: The passage says there will be “a cloud and smoke by day.”
easy.q: What will appear by day over Mount Zion?

answers: The shining of a flaming fire
easy.explanation: At night there will be “the shining of a flaming fire.”
The tabernacle will be a shadow from heat and a refuge from storm and rain.
easy.q: What will the tabernacle provide protection from?

answers: To display glory and provide protection
To provide food and illuminate the earth
To punish the remnant and scatter it
medium.explanation: The covering is connected with “all the glory” and also serves as a shelter.
medium.q: What is the twofold purpose of the divine covering?

medium.explanation: Here, “tabernacle” refers to a shelter or covering.
medium.q: What does “a tabernacle” mean in this context?

answers: By day there is cloud and smoke, and by night a flaming fire
By day there is fire, and by night there is fruit
By day there is rain, and by night there is judgment
medium.explanation: Verse 5 names cloud and smoke by day and the shining of a flaming fire by night.
medium.q: How does the description of protection differ between day and night?

answers: The glory over Zion is accompanied by protective covering
Glory removes the need for any shelter
challenge.explanation: The passage says that upon all the glory there shall be a defense.
challenge.q: How are glory and defense connected in the passage?

answers: The shelter provides protection in varied conditions
The shelter is intended only for nighttime
challenge.explanation: The several dangers named show that the refuge is broad and practical.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from protection against heat, storm, and rain?

answers: They present a visible, continuing sign by day and night
They show that the city is abandoned
challenge.explanation: The signs appear by day and night over Zion, conveying continuing divine presence and protection.
challenge.q: How do the cloud and fire reinforce the idea of God's presence?

short_answers.question: What will the tabernacle be for during the day?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 6 says it will be “a tabernacle for a shadow in the day time from the heat.”
